title: Shmashan mein Mahavira Swami ko Yaksha ne kaise pariksha di?
hooks: Shmashan ki raat... Mahavira Swami kayotsarga mein.
Ek Yaksha aaya, unki samta todne — kya hua?
Raat bhar aag, bhoot, sher... Swami hile tak nahi.
hook_why: Opens with named entity (Mahavira Swami) and place (shmashan) in first 4 words — matches raaz hook rule. Visual of meditating idol in cremation ground creates immediate kinetic curiosity without audio.
metaphor: A single white marble idol standing unmoved while illusions (fire, ghosts, beasts) swirl around like smoke — the still center proves inner victory.
mechanism: Yaksha creates illusion of fire to test fear
Mahavira's kayotsarga remains unbroken — fire cannot touch inner stillness
Ghost army appears with terrifying sounds — tests attachment to safety
Single-pointed gaze (drishti) dissolves illusions — no reaction, no flinch
Wild animals (lion, snake, elephant) approach — test instinctive survival fear
Each beast fades like mist — proves they were mental projections
Yaksha reveals true divine form — acknowledges victory of samta
Declares 'Samkitva jeeta, moh haar gaya' — right faith conquers delusion
Lesson: true tapasya is internal equanimity, not external austerity

cast.Mahavira Swami: serene white marble temple idol in kayotsarga (standing meditation), eyes half-closed, lion emblem on pedestal, plain unadorned, warm golden light
cast.Yaksha: divine nature spirit in ancient Indian attire, calm face, simple ornaments, glowing gently, not fearsome

scenes.vo: Shmashan ki raat... Mahavira Swami kayotsarga mein khade the.
scenes.prompt: Night cremation ground (shmashan) with ancient Jain temple shikhara spires silhouetted against starry sky. Center: white marble idol of Mahavira Swami in kayotsarga (standing meditation), eyes half-closed, lion emblem on pedestal. Warm golden moonlight on marble. Serene painterly Indian style, calm, uncluttered. No Hindu icons, no onion domes.
scenes.title: Shmashan ki raat

scenes.vo: Ek Yaksha aaya, unki samta todne.
scenes.prompt: Same shmashan scene. A divine Yaksha figure appears at edge of frame — ancient Indian attire, calm face, simple ornaments, gentle glow. He observes the meditating idol. Warm golden light, serene painterly style. No weapons, no fearsome features.
scenes.title: Yaksha ki pariksha

scenes.vo: Pehle aag ki lein uthai, charon taraf se gher liya.
scenes.prompt: Flames rise around the marble idol — orange-red fire licking the air, but the idol remains untouched, serene. Camera tilts up following flames. Warm golden firelight contrasts cool marble. Painterly style, no horror aesthetic.
scenes.title: Aag ka mayajaal

scenes.vo: Par Mahavira Swami hile nahi, samadhi sthir rahi.
scenes.prompt: Close on marble idol face — eyes half-closed, utterly still. Firelight flickers on white stone. Zero movement. Serene, painterly, warm golden glow. Pull back slowly to show full kayotsarga figure unmoved.
scenes.title: Sthir samadhi

scenes.vo: Phir bhooton ki sena aayi, bhaayanak awaazein machayi.
scenes.prompt: Shadowy ghostly forms swirl around idol — translucent, painterly, not grotesque. They make silent screaming gestures. Idol unchanged. Warm golden light from within marble pushes shadows back. Serene, not scary.
scenes.title: Bhooton ki sena

scenes.vo: Swami ki drishti nahi doli, shwas tak ek samaan.
scenes.prompt: Extreme close-up of idol's half-closed eyes. Single tear of light? No — just stillness. Breath suggested by faintest shimmer of golden air. Magnifier match-cut: push into eye, hard-cut to 3x magnified same angle showing micro-detail of carved eyelid. Painterly, reverent.
scenes.title: Akhand drishti

scenes.vo: Sher, saanp, haathi... sab aaye, sab gaye, jaise dhuaan.
scenes.prompt: Centered composition: a serene Jain idol on a pedestal, with a calm lion, a coiled snake, and a gentle elephant appearing one by one around it, each rendered as living animals in soft golden light, peaceful and non‑aggressive. Warm golden sunrise illumination, ample space above and below for text. No text or logos.
scenes.title: Sher Saanp Haathi

scenes.vo: Yaksha ne asli roop dikhaya, pranam kiya.
scenes.prompt: Yaksha now stands revealed — radiant, peaceful, hands folded in namaste before the idol. Divine glow. Marble idol unchanged. Warm golden light from both figures meets. Serene painterly Indian style, ancient temple architecture background.
scenes.title: Yaksha ka naman

scenes.prompt: Plain warm marble texture background. Subtle golden glow. No text.

scenes.vo: Sachcha tap bahar ka nahi, andar ka jeet hai.
scenes.prompt: Wide shot of an ancient Jain temple at dawn, white marble shikharas, carved pillars, stepped roofs (Dilwara style), golden sunrise light, single kayotsarga idol on plinth, peaceful and uncluttered. Pull back to reveal scale. No text or logos.
scenes.title: Sachcha Tap

scenes.vo: Aap hote toh kya karte? Jai Jinendra.
scenes.title: Jai Jinendra

caption: Shmashan mein raat bhar tap... Yaksha ne kya dekha? Kalpasutra ki yeh katha samta ka sach batati hai. Aap hote toh kya karte? #Mahavira #Kalpasutra #JainKatha #Samta #NavkarBhav

claims.claim: Mahavira Swami stayed in a cremation ground (shmashan) during his ascetic period and was tested by a Yaksha.
claims.basis: Kalpasutra (Lives of the Jinas) by Bhadrabahu — contains biography of Mahavira including his 12 years of asceticism and trials.

claims.claim: The Yaksha created illusions of fire, ghosts, and wild animals to disturb Mahavira's meditation.
claims.basis: Kalpasutra account of Mahavira's trials (pariksha) during kayotsarga in shmashan.

claims.claim: Mahavira remained unmoved in kayotsarga (standing meditation) throughout all tests.
claims.basis: Kalpasutra — central theme of samta (equanimity) as highest tap.

claims.claim: The Yaksha finally revealed his true form, bowed, and declared 'Samkitva jeeta, moh haar gaya' (Right faith won, delusion lost).
claims.basis: Kalpasutra narrative of Yaksha's submission after witnessing unshakable samta.

claims.claim: Source is Kalpasutra, ascribed to Acharya Bhadrabahu, a Cheda Sutra of Shvetambara canon.
claims.basis: Wikipedia, Wisdom Library, Hinduwebsite.com — all confirm Kalpasutra authorship and content.
